Corrections and removal requests

By the RadioReach editorial team Published August 19, 2026 Reviewed August 19, 2026

If something on this site or in the Radio Reach Vault is wrong, tell us and we will fix it. Station staff can have their details corrected or removed without giving a reason, and we act on removal requests in the next compilation pass. Material corrections to published pages are logged on this page rather than quietly edited.

On this page
  • How to report a problem
  • Station contact removal
  • What we commit to
  • Correction log

How to report a problem

We want reports of four things in particular: a factual error in a guide, an out-of-date or incorrect contact record, a contact that should not be listed at all, and any claim on this site that you think we cannot support. That last category is genuinely welcome — if our marketing overstates the product, we would rather hear it from you than from a regulator.

Include the page URL or the station name, what is wrong, and what the correct information is if you know it. Use the contact route on our About page.

If you work at a station and want your details removed

You do not need to explain why, prove harm, or send a legal notice. Tell us the station and the contact detail, and we will remove it. We will confirm once it is done, and the removal is applied to the compilation so it does not reappear in a later pass.

If your details are wrong rather than unwanted — a former staff member listed in your role, an old submissions address — we would rather correct the record than delete it, because artists will keep looking for a route to your station either way. Either outcome is your call, not ours.

What we commit to

  • Acknowledgement of any correction or removal request when we receive it.
  • Removal requests actioned in the next compilation pass, with confirmation.
  • Factual errors on published pages fixed promptly, with the page's reviewed date updated to the date a human actually made the fix.
  • Material corrections logged publicly below. A material correction is one that changes the meaning of a claim — a wrong number, a wrong statement about what the product includes, a wrong statement about a competitor. Typos and formatting fixes are not logged.
  • No silent edits to claims we previously made and can no longer support.

Correction log

DateWhereCorrection
2026-08-19 Sales page, checkout, adaptive copy, conversion experiments Removed claims that a specific number of email addresses were "individually verified deliverable addresses". No documented deliverability check had been run against the shipping file, so the word "verified" was being used as a synonym for "included". Replaced with a description of what the records actually contain. See our definitions.
2026-08-19 Customer testimonials Removed "Verified buyer" badges. RadioReach has no verified-purchase review system, so the badge implied a check that did not exist.
2026-08-19 Terms of service, refund copy The terms page said digital sales were "generally final" while the checkout promised a 30-day refund. The 30-day refund is the binding policy; the terms were corrected to match.
2026-08-19 Pricing comparison copy Removed the claim that the file is "the same caliber of data" as $300–$500/year enterprise media databases. The comparison was unsupported; the price contrast is now stated without the equivalence claim.
2026-08-19 Site footer Copyright named the product ("Radio Reach Vault") as the publishing organisation. Corrected to RadioReach, with an explicit statement of non-affiliation with listed stations.

Limitations of this page

This log begins on 19 August 2026, when the correction policy was published. Corrections made before that date were not systematically recorded, so the absence of earlier entries reflects the absence of a log rather than the absence of errors.
